data.description:
## Goal

Parse and validate `games/manifest.json` and decide, per entry, whether the game is compatible with the launcher's core-engine version — as a pure, browser/Electron-agnostic module with unit tests.

## Context

Part of FEATURE: Electron runtime game plugin loader (CG-0MTRO7VMI000F3A5). Realises AC1 (runtime game discovery metadata) and AC2 (core version compatibility check). Must not throw on malformed input — it returns a structured result so the launcher can degrade gracefully (AC4).

## Manifest schema (authoritative for this item)

```json
{
  "version": 1,
  "games": [
    {
      "id": "golf",
      "sceneKey": "GolfScene",
      "title": "9-Card Golf",
      "description": "Lowest score wins.",
      "thumbnail": "assets/thumbnail.png",
      "coreEngineVersion": "^0.1.0",
      "entry": "entry.js"
    }
  ]
}
```

## Acceptance Criteria

- **Core version compatibility check** — Each game declares a `coreEngineVersion` (semver range) in its manifest; the launcher checks compatibility at load time and skips incompatible games with a clear error message in the Game Selector UI.
- **Core version compatibility check** — `parseGameManifest(json: string | unknown)` returns a discriminated result: `{ ok: true, manifest }` or `{ ok: false, errors: string[] }`; it never throws on malformed JSON or a wrong shape.
- Each entry is validated for required fields (`id`, `sceneKey`, `title`, `description`, `coreEngineVersion`, `entry`) with field-named error messages; duplicate `id` or `sceneKey` values are rejected.
- `splitByCompatibility(entries, engineVersion)` returns `{ compatible, incompatible }`, where each incompatible item carries a human-readable reason naming the required range and the launcher version.
- A `coreEngineVersion` semver range is honoured via the `semver` package (`semver.satisfies`); invalid ranges are reported as validation errors, not thrown.
- The launcher's engine version is exposed by the core engine (single source of truth) and consumed by the compatibility check.
- Unit tests cover every AC above, including missing manifest, malformed JSON, missing fields, duplicate ids, incompatible range, and invalid range.

## Minimal Implementation

- Add `src/ui/game-manifest.ts`: types (`GameManifest`, `GameManifestEntry`), `parseGameManifest`, `splitByCompatibility`, `DEFAULT_ENGINE_VERSION`.
- Add `semver` (+ `@types/semver`) to `dependencies`.
- Export the engine version constant from `@core-engine` and reuse it.
- Tests in `tests/ui/game-manifest.test.ts` using the F1 fixtures.

## Key Files

- `src/ui/game-manifest.ts`
- `src/core-engine/index.ts`
- `package.json`
- `tests/ui/game-manifest.test.ts`

## Dependencies

- F1 loader test harness & fixture.
data.title: Manifest parser & core-version compatibility

data.description:
## Goal

Resolve game-specific assets (thumbnails and other files) relative to each game's artifact directory, and serve them safely to the Electron renderer under a packaged `file://`/asar build — realising AC3 (asset resolution).

## Context

Part of FEATURE: Electron runtime game plugin loader (CG-0MTRO7VMI000F3A5). `GameSelectorScene` currently loads `assets/<thumbnail>.png` from the launcher's own `public/` root; runtime games must instead resolve from `<contentDir>/games/<id>/…`. Direct `file://` image loads from arbitrary content dirs can hit CORS/canvas-taint and path issues, so a scoped custom protocol is introduced.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **Asset resolution** — Thumbnails and other game-specific assets are resolved relative to the game's artifact location (not relative to the launcher's `public/` directory).
- **Asset resolution** — A pure resolver `resolveGameAssetUrl(gameId, relativePath)` returns a `tce-games://<id>/<normalised-path>` URL, rejecting any path that escapes the game directory (`..`, absolute paths, `\0`).
- The Electron main process registers a `tce-games://` protocol (privileged/`standard` + `secure`) that resolves requests only inside `<contentDir>/games/`; requests outside that root return `404`/are denied.
- The protocol handler is Electron-free-unit-testable via an injectable file reader/resolver (no Electron import in the pure logic).
- MIME types are set for at least `.png`; unknown extensions are served as `application/octet-stream`.
- Unit tests cover the resolver (valid, traversal, encoded traversal) and the protocol path-resolution logic.

## Minimal Implementation

- Add `src/ui/game-asset-url.ts` with `resolveGameAssetUrl` + `resolveAssetFilePath(contentDir, requestUrl)`.
- Register the protocol in `electron/main.ts` before window creation (`protocol.handle`), reusing the resolver.
- Tests in `tests/ui/game-asset-url.test.ts` and `tests/electron/game-protocol.test.ts`.

## Key Files

- `src/ui/game-asset-url.ts`
- `electron/main.ts`
- `tests/ui/game-asset-url.test.ts`
- `tests/electron/game-protocol.test.ts`

## Dependencies

- F1 loader test harness & fixture.
data.title: Asset resolution & tce-games protocol

data.description:
The current `deploy.yml` workflow runs `npm run build`, which defaults to the `core-only` preset (Gym only). To deploy the full distribution with all games, the workflow must select the all-games preset via `GAMES_CONFIG`.

## Problem

The GitHub Pages deployment only publishes the Gym (core engine demo), not the full set of example games listed in `configs/full.json`.

## Solution

Update the "Build" step in `.github/workflows/deploy.yml` to select the all-games preset:

```yaml
- name: Build
  run: GAMES_CONFIG=full npm run build
```

The config-driven game discovery plugin (`scripts/vite-game-discovery-plugin.ts`) reads `configs/full.json`, which lists all 8 games. Each game is resolved locally first (`example-games/<id>/...`) then as a sibling repo (`../tce-<id>/...`), so this works whether building from the launcher checkout or from a single-game repo.

> **Preset name corrected (plan, 2026-09-26):** this item originally referenced `GAMES_CONFIG=all` / `configs/all.json`. No such preset exists anywhere in the repository. `selectConfigPath()` treats an unknown preset name as a **hard error** (deliberately: it never silently falls back, because that would ship a distribution missing the requested games), so a literal implementation of the original wording would break the Pages build. The canonical "every game" preset is **`full`** (`configs/full.json`) — evidenced by `README.md`, `docs/DEVELOPER.md#config-driven-game-catalogue`, `configs/full.json`'s own `$comment`, CG-0MTRO77XA006YZZC AC5 (`full=all`), and `tests/scripts/distribution-presets.test.ts` which pins the named-preset contract. The author's intent ("deploy all games") is unchanged; only the mechanism name is corrected. See "OPEN QUESTION" in the comments.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1:** The `deploy.yml` Build step selects the all-games preset (`GAMES_CONFIG=full`) so the production build includes all 8 games listed in `configs/full.json`.
- **AC2:** A local build with `GAMES_CONFIG=full` completes successfully (`npm run build` with the environment variable set).
- **AC3:** The resulting `dist/` contains the unified launcher with all 8 games plus the Gym selectable from the landing page.
- **AC4:** `RELEASE.md` describes the deploy build step consistently with the workflow (same-commit doc update, per the project doc-update policy for CI/CD changes).
- **AC5:** A regression test pins the deploy workflow's preset selection so it cannot silently revert to the `core-only` default (the defect this item fixes).

## Key Files

- `.github/workflows/deploy.yml` — CI deployment workflow (one-line change)
- `configs/full.json` — already exists, lists all 8 games
- `scripts/vite-game-discovery-plugin.ts` — reads `GAMES_CONFIG` to discover games
- `RELEASE.md` — deploy workflow description (doc-update policy)
- `tests/scripts/deploy-workflow.test.ts` — new regression test (filename indicative)

## Outline

1. Add the regression test pinning the all-games preset on the deploy Build step (test-first; fails against the current workflow).
2. Set `GAMES_CONFIG=full` on the `deploy.yml` Build step.
3. Update `RELEASE.md` so its description of the deploy workflow matches.
4. Verify: `GAMES_CONFIG=full npm run build` exits 0 and `dist/`'s game selector catalogue contains all 8 games plus the Gym.

## Verification notes

- Deleting the `GAMES_CONFIG` assignment must fail the new regression test.
- `GAMES_CONFIG=all` must still hard-fail the build (proves the corrected preset name is the only working mechanism); no `configs/all.json` alias is to be created, since a duplicate preset would conflict with the preset contract pinned by CG-0MTRO77XA006YZZC.
data.title: Deploy full engine with all games via GAMES_CONFIG=all
